theory.intro: Since $180^{\circ} = \pi\text{ radians}$, multiply degrees by $\dfrac{\pi}{180^{\circ}}$ to get radians, and multiply radians by $\dfrac{180^{\circ}}{\pi}$ to get degrees. Degree-to-radian answers requested in terms of $\pi$ are written as simplified fractions of $\pi$.
facts: **Degrees to radians**: multiply by $\dfrac{\pi}{180^{\circ}}$ and simplify the fraction: $\text{rad} = \text{deg} \times \dfrac{\pi}{180}$.
When converting a $\pi$-fraction from radians to degrees, substitute $180^{\circ}$ directly in place of $\pi$.
If an angle does not have a degree symbol ($^{\circ}$), it is assumed to be in radians.
When converting degrees to radians in terms of $\pi$, leave the answer as a simplified multiple or fraction of $\pi$ (e.g. $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$), not a decimal approximation.
steps: Identify the starting unit (degrees or radians)
Multiply by the conversion factor $\frac{\pi}{180^{\circ}}$ or $\frac{180^{\circ}}{\pi}$
Simplify the fraction or round as requested

workedExamples.question_text:
Convert each angle to radians as a simplified fraction of $\pi$.
(a) $67.5^{\circ}$
(b) $585^{\circ}$
(c) $-210^{\circ}$
workedExamples.solution_text:
Multiply each degree measure by $\dfrac{\pi}{180^{\circ}}$. Keep the sign and any complete revolutions.
(a) $\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}67.5^{\circ}\times\dfrac{\pi}{180^{\circ}}\\&=\dfrac{67.5\pi}{180}\\&=\dfrac{3\pi}{8}\text{ rad}\end{aligned}$
(b) $\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}585^{\circ}\times\dfrac{\pi}{180^{\circ}}\\&=\dfrac{585\pi}{180}\\&=\dfrac{13\pi}{4}\text{ rad}\end{aligned}$
(c) $\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}-210^{\circ}\times\dfrac{\pi}{180^{\circ}}\\&=-\dfrac{210\pi}{180}\\&=-\dfrac{7\pi}{6}\text{ rad}\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text:
Convert each angle to degrees, giving exact answers.
(a) $\dfrac{9\pi}{8}\text{ radians}$
(b) $-\dfrac{13\pi}{6}\text{ radians}$

Convert these angles to degrees.
(a) $0.8\text{ radians}$, correct to the nearest degree.
(b) $2.6\text{ radians}$, correct to $1$ decimal place.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Multiply by $\dfrac{180^{\circ}}{\pi}$, using the calculator's full value of $\pi$. Round only the final answer.
(a) $\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}0.8\times\dfrac{180^{\circ}}{\pi}\\&=\dfrac{144^{\circ}}{\pi}\\&\approx45.8366^{\circ}\\&\approx46^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
(b) $\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}2.6\times\dfrac{180^{\circ}}{\pi}\\&=\dfrac{468^{\circ}}{\pi}\\&\approx148.9690^{\circ}\\&\approx149.0^{\circ}\end{aligned}$
